result.title: RxnExBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Structured Chemical Reaction Extraction from Scientific Literature
result.summary: Screen Tables and Substrate Scopes are information-dense figures widely used in synthetic chemistry literature, yet automated extraction of structured reaction data from them remains challenging. We introduce RxnExBench, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained reaction-level evaluation. Built from high-impact chemistry journals, it contains 3,565 expert-annotated reactions and 2,361 molecular structures. The dataset adopts a unified schema with 15 reaction roles and 26 core fields, supporting downstream AI-for-Chemistry tasks such as retrosynthetic planning, yield prediction, and reaction condition recommendation. RxnExBench further provides a reasoning-driven difficulty taxonomy, a modular annotation pipeline, and the Oracle-MolRec protocol, which disentangles molecular recognition from higher-level reasoning. Evaluation of 9 state-of-the-art VLMs shows that performance degrades substantially as schema complexity and reasoning demands increase. Under the Oracle-MolRec setting, results further reveal that accurate molecular recognition alone is insufficient, with multimodal integration and chemistry-aware reasoning remaining the primary bottlenecks. We release all data and code to facilitate future research in chemistry-aware multimodal understanding and AI-for-Chemistry dataset construction. The dataset and code will be released at https://github.com/opendatalab/RxnExBench.

AI.brief_summary: 构建化学文献中信息密集图（Screen Tables、Substrate Scopes）的结构化反应抽取基准 RxnExBench，含 3565 个专家标注反应与 2361 个分子结构，采用 15 种反应角色、26 个核心字段的统一模式，并提供难度分类、标注流程与可分离分子识别与高层推理的 Oracle-MolRec 协议；9 个 VLM 评测显示模式复杂度与推理需求上升时性能明显下降。
AI.relevance_reason: Oracle-MolRec 将视觉识别与高阶推理分解评测的做法，可供核查细粒度视觉细节保留与「识别 vs 推理」贡献分配的诊断设计，但本身是化学抽取基准而非 LVR 机制研究。
